2289946.title: Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions
2289946.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Safe & Trusted AI Pillar under IndiaAI Mission Strengthens Citizen Trust through Secure, Fair and Responsible AI Solutions
13 Responsible AI Projects, 58 AI Centres of Excellence and 27 India Data & AI Labs Strengthen Safe & Trusted AI under IndiaAI Mission
India's Safe & Trusted AI Pillar Powers Responsible Innovation while Shaping Global AI Governance
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

IndiaAI Mission: India’s AI policy is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of democratizing technology. It is aimed at creating economic opportunities and employment for youth, while addressing risks associated with AI.

 

Accordingly, the Government approved the IndiaAI Mission in March 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371 crore over five years to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in the country.

 

The Mission comprises seven pillars viz. IndiaAI Compute, Foundation Models, AIKosh, IndiaAI

Application Development Initiative, FutureSkills, Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI.

 

Progress under IndiaAI mission till date:

 

AI models: Government of India is supporting Indian startups and institutions to develop large language models. 20 indigenous sovereign model proposals have been identified for support, comprising 12 LLMs and 8 SLMs. Notable successes so far include:

  • Sarvam AI’s Sarvam 30 billion parameter and 105 billion parameter models
  • Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model
  • BharatGen’s multilingual foundation models
  • Avataar AI’s video generation model

 

Domain-specific SLMs, including specialized models and AI frameworks addressing healthcare, language technologies and agentic AI systems are at various stages of development and deployment.

 

Affordable compute:

  • Compute service providers empanelled: 15
  • Number of projects supported: 237
  • GPU hours sanctioned: 93 lakh GPU hours
     

Application Development:

  • 12 National-level Hackathons/Innovation Challenges launched.
  • Supported the development of 62 AI prototypes and 20 AI solutions deployment
     

Talent development:

  • 686 fellowships have been awarded across undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes in 178 institutions.
  • YUVA AI for All programme has been completed by over 26 lakh individuals.
     

IndiaAI labs:

  • 27 India Data and AI Labs have been established, which has supported training for more than 2500 students
  • Work ongoing on additional 188 labs.

 

AI Centres of Excellence:

58 Artificial Intelligence Centres of Excellence (AI-CoEs) being established across States and Union Territories in collaboration with the respective State/UT Governments and industry partners.

 

Safe & Trusted AI pillar

At the same time, the Government is also cognizant of the risks associated with AI. The Safe & Trusted AI pillar of the IndiaAI Mission aims to promote the responsible development, deployment and adoption of AI through indigenous governance frameworks, standards, tools and evaluation mechanisms.

 

13 Responsible AI projects have been approved in educational institutions across the country. These include topics such as bias mitigation, machine unlearning, privacy-preserving AI, explainability, deepfake detection and AI risk assessment.

 

Key initiatives include:

  • Saakshya, multi-agent framework developed by IIT Jodhpur &  IIT Madras for deep fake detection
  • AI Vishleshak for improving Audio-Visual forgery detection system
  • IIT Kharagpur’s project on Real-Time Voice Deepfake Detection System

 

Nature & Objectives of projects related to bias mitigation, explainability, privacy preserving Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning:

  • Bias Mitigation: NIT Raipur is developing responsible AI algorithms to reduce bias in medical image analysis, clinical decision-making and healthcare applications
  • Privacy-Preserving & Explainable AI: IIT Delhi (with IIIT Delhi and IIT Dharwad) is developing privacy-preserving machine learning models using federated learning.
    • Defence Institute of Advanced Technology (DIAT) is is building explainable & privacy-preserving AI for security applications
  • Machine Unlearning: IIT Jodhpur is developing techniques to remove remove unwanted, sensitive or outdated information/concepts from generative foundation models

 

Overall, these projects are aimed at making AI fairer, more transparent, privacy-preserving, secure and trustworthy.

•  The AI Safety Institute has been established for AI safety, security and developing trust with diverse stakeholders, engaging academia, startups, industry and Government bodies through a hub-and-spoke model.

• The India AI Governance Guidelines lay down a risk-based governance framework addressing algorithmic bias, misinformation, deepfakes and unintended societal harm, and propose institutional mechanisms including the AI Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG), Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) and AI Safety Institute (AISI) for oversight, standards and safety research.

 

The IndiaAI Safety Institute was announced in January 2025 to advance science-based and indigenous research on AI safety and governance. The Institute is responsible for promoting the safe, secure, inclusive and trustworthy development, deployment and adoption of AI in India.

 

It also oversees the implementation of projects selected under the two rounds of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar.

 

India's approach to responsible AI is anchored in the vision of "AI for All". It seeks to harness AI for inclusive development while ensuring that it remains safe, trusted, and aligned with India's socio-economic priorities.

  • India actively engages with global processes on AI governance, including Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), G20, and United Nations, to ensure that international norms reflect the perspectives and priorities of the Global South
  • As Chair of the India AI Impact Summit 2026, held in New Delhi, India contributed in shaping the global agenda on responsible AI through key deliverables:
    • As part of New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments, leading AI developers made voluntary commitments on the safe and responsible development of frontier AI
    • Guidance Note on AI Governance, oﬀered practical guidance to countries on designing context-appropriate AI governance frameworks
    • Trusted AI Commons, a shared repository of open resources to democratise access to safe and trusted AI

 

These outcomes reflect India's commitment to shaping global norms on AI governance while protecting its strategic and developmental interests.

 

This information was submitted by Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Rajya Sabha on 24.07.2026.

2289945.title: EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC
2289945.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
EXPANSION OF HEALTHCARE FACILITIES BY ESIC
Over 1.38 lakh new employers and more than 1.12 lakh new employees added under SPREE Scheme between July 2025 and January 2026
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has launched the Scheme to Promote Registration of Employers/Employees (SPREE 2025) from July 2025 to January 2026.  Under the Scheme, a one-time opportunity was provided to employers and employees of organised sectors who may have been inadvertently left out from ESI coverage to register without concern for retrospective coverage or punitive action. A total of 1,38,718 new employers and 1,12,72,772 employees have been added during the Scheme till 31.01.2026.

ESIC has undertaken several initiatives across the country to strengthen healthcare infrastructure, improve access to quality medical services and enhance social security benefits for ESI beneficiaries. These include enhancement of bed strength, procurement of advanced medical equipment, establishment of ICU/HDU facilities, operationalisation of new hospitals and dispensaries, empanelment of private and super-specialty hospitals, upgradation of digital platforms for OPD appointments, Aadhaar-based authentication for delivery of benefits, online submission of cash benefit claims, collaboration with Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) for providing secondary and tertiary healthcare services where ESIC facilities are not adequately available.

ESIC has also recently operationalised/upgraded hospitals at Ompora (Jammu & Kashmir), Doddaballapur (Karnataka), Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu), Surat (Gujarat), and expanded hospitals at Sanath Nagar (Telangana), Beltola (Assam) and Rajamahendravaram (Andhra Pradesh).

This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2289944.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
ATAL BEEMIT VYAKTI KALYAN YOJANA
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has approved extension of the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) from 01.07.2026 to 30.06.2027.

The eligibility criteria to avail benefit under the Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) is as under:

  1. The insured person must be in insurable employment for a minimum period of 12 months immediately before his/her unemployment and should have contributed for not less than 78 days in one completed contribution period in 12 months immediately preceding to unemployment.
  2. The unemployment must not arise from misconduct, during lock out, superannuation, or convicted for false statement under the provision of ESI Act, 1948.

Several steps to expedite the settlement of claim under the scheme have been taken. These include online submission and processing of the claims, direct benefit transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of beneficiaries and regular monitoring of claim settlement to ensure timely disbursal of benefits.

2289931.title: KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT
2289931.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
KOSI-MECHI INTRA-STATE LINK PROJECT
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Kosi–Mechi Intra-State Link Project has been included under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayi Yojana – Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (PMKSY-AIBP) for balance cost of works of Rs. 6,143.22 crore, with central assistance of Rs. 3,652.56 crore. The project is scheduled for completion by March 2029.  The remodeling work of Eastern Kosi Main Canal from K.M. 0.00 to 41.30 has been taken up at an awarded contract value Rs. 2639.80 crore.  Physical progress of 8.5% has been achieved so far.

The Government of India is engaged in regular dialogue with the Government of Nepal regarding construction of dams on the Kosi River for the mutual benefit of both countries, including flood control. A Joint Project Office (JPO-SKSKI) was constituted in 2003 with the mandate to prepare the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Sapta-Kosi Multipurpose Project and Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project. The status of preparation the DPRs of these projects is as under.

  1. Sapta Kosi Multipurpose Project: The work of topographical surveys, construction material survey, water quality survey, inland navigation studies, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,258m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed.

  2. Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project: The work of topographical surveys, water quality survey, hydrological studies, seismological studies, drilling (1,549m), communication survey, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) studies have been completed for Sun-Kosi Kamla Diversion Multipurpose project.

Further, no meeting of Indo-Nepal Joint Committee was held during 2025-26.

Central assistance of Rs. 206.77 Crore has been released to the State of Bihar under the Flood Management and Border Areas Programme during last three years.

No proposal for a permanent Kosi-Gandak basin authority is under consideration of the Government of India.

The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

   “MUSEUM GRANT SCHEME AND PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE”
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Culture operates Museum Grant Scheme under which financial assistance is provided for setting up of New Museums/development of the existing museums/digitization of museum collections/setting up of virtual museums and training of museums professionals of museums managed by Central/State Governments, Societies, Autonomous bodies, Public sector Undertaking, local bodies, Academic Institutions and Trusts registered under the societies Act at the regional, State and District Level in the country.

Eligibility Criteria: For the purpose of support under this component, museums have been classified into three categories as per the existing guidelines of the Museum Grant Scheme:

 

  1. Category I: Central or State Government owned museums in State Capitals including Museums owned by Public Sector Undertakings.
  2. Category II: Central or State Govt. owned museums including Museums of Public Sector Undertakings
  3. Category III: All other museums including Museums of Public Sector Undertakings

Category I: Existing renowned Museums of the Central or State Governments located in the state capitals, subject to the following:

  1. The museum must be located in the capital of the state/union territory.
  2. It must be of high repute, having a significant collection of objects/artefacts.
  3. It must have had an annual footfall of 1 lakh visitors per annum in the preceding 2 years.

Category II: Central or State Govt. owned museums including museums of PSU

Category III: Projects of Societies, Autonomous bodies, local bodies, Public Sector Undertaking, Academic Institutions and Trusts registered as a society under the Indian Societies Act of 1860 (XXI) or a similar legislation of the state governments, or as a Public Trust under any law at the time being in force subject to the following:

  1. It should have been in existence for at least three years prior to the application. However, this condition can be relaxed in exceptional cases at the discretion of the Expert Committee, the reasons for which should be recorded in writing;
  2. It should have a well-defined constitution and laid down rules/bye laws for its   functioning
  3.  It should be in ownership and possession of a substantial collection of objects of historical and / or cultural importance for display in the museum.
  4. It should be able to maintain the Museum and bear all recurring costs;
  5. It should have the necessary infrastructural facilities, resources and     personnel to execute the work for which the grant is required;
  6. It should produce a certificate from the State Government (Department of   Culture or equivalent) attesting to its satisfactory performance;
  7. It should not be run for personal profit.
  8. It should be the owner of the land on which the museum is situated or proposed to be constructed, which should be easily accessible to visitors. 

 

Ministry of Culture, Government of India may take up   any project under Category I &II as project of National importance at its discretion for the purpose of development of Museum & Cultural Spaces.

Under the Museum Grant Scheme financial assistance is being provided to:

 

  1. Museums having collection of Antiquities, Numismatics, Paintings, Ethnological collections, Fold Art and others including Art & Crafts, Textiles, Stamps etc.
  2. Online Virtual Museums displaying objects in any or all the disciplines and
  3. Theme based Museums
  4. Virtual Experiential Museums
  5. Projects of National Importance.

 

Ministry of Culture provides financial assistance to the project proposals received for digitalisation of museum collections as per guidelines of the Museum Grant Scheme.

 

Further, The Ministry of Tourism promotes India as a holistic destination in the tourism generating markets to promote various Indian tourism products and tourism destinations of the country, including Museums, to increase India’s share of the global tourism market. The promotion is carried out through organizing and participating in travel events and exhibitions; providing assistance to State Governments for organizing fairs and festivals; inviting influencers, tour operators, journalists and opinion makers to visit the country under the Hospitality Programme of the Ministry; various outreach activities through website and social media; promotions in association with the State Governments and the overseas Indian Missions etc.

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

2289927.title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT
2289927.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS OF THE KALPASAR PROJECT
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

As informed by the Government of Gujarat, the proposed Gulf of Khambhat (Kalpasar) Project is an ambitious water resources initiatives of the State Government. The project envisages the creation of one of the world's largest coastal freshwater reservoirs through the construction of a dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. Upon implementation, the project is expected to significantly augment the availability of freshwater and substantially mitigate water scarcity in the Saurashtra region by providing a dependable source of water for irrigation and other identified uses.

The project includes a proposed highway-cum-rail corridor over the dam across the Gulf of Khambhat. As per the present project layout, the corridor is expected to reduce the travel distance between Bhavnagar and Surat by approximately 179 km, from about 356 km through the existing land route to about 177 km via the proposed dyke corridor, thereby improving regional connectivity and reducing travel time.

As informed by the State Government of Gujarat, Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Kalpasar Project is at an advanced stage of finalization. The ongoing Indo-Dutch technical cooperation is expected to further strengthen the DPR by incorporating international best practices and advanced technical expertise in areas such as coastal engineering, hydraulic modelling, salinity management, climate resilience and water management. This collaboration is intended to enhance the technical robustness of the project and facilitate informed decision-making during its implementation.

The project envisages development of approximately 2,470 MW of hybrid renewable energy capacity on reclaimed land that is presently submerged during high tide. The renewable energy generated is proposed to be utilized, inter alia, for pumping freshwater to meet irrigation requirements in the coastal regions of Saurashtra. DPR incorporates appropriate engineering measures, hydraulic studies and salinity management strategies to address the issue of salinity ingress.

The information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

The details of the Museums, Memorials and interpretation centres dedicated to the Indian freedom movement, freedom fighters and the national independence struggle is given at Annexure.

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) undertakes maintenance and upgradation of museums and exhibitions relating to India's freedom movement, subject to requirement. ASI organises outreach programmes on important occasions such as Independence Day, Republic Day, World Heritage Day and Week and International Museum Day, in association with local schools, educational institutions and heritage stakeholders, to create awareness among children and youth about the legacy of India's freedom movement. 

Further, various programmes/exhibitions are carried out throughout the year as per the events in the museums of the Ministry of Culture to preserve and promote the legacy of India's freedom movement.

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

2289921.title: Gyan Bharatam Mission and Manuscript Digitisation
2289921.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Gyan Bharatam Mission and Manuscript Digitisation
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, National Manuscript Survey was launched across all States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. However, any district-wise target was not set for the survey and physical registration of manuscripts under the Mission. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported.

 Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses AI (Artificial Intelligence) enabled technologies, including Large Language Script Models (LLSM), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR), script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation, to provide intelligent access to India’s manuscript heritage.

Gyan Mitram, the AI-powered knowledge interface of the Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses LLSM, OCR, HTR, script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation to enable intelligent interpretation, contextualization and exploration of manuscripts by integrating manuscript images, transcriptions and translations.

BharatiyaGPT, features “Manuscript-to-Conversational AI” on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal converting manuscript heritage into AI-ready, machine-readable knowledge and provides a multilingual and multimodal access, including text, audio and voice-based interaction through its “Talk to Manuscript” feature, thereby making India’s knowledge traditions more accessible to scholars, students, researchers and the public.

 

Pandulipi Darpan is an AI driven tool on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal that enables users to upload or select a digitized manuscript image and access AI-assisted script recognition, transliteration and translation.


Access to digitized copies of manuscript is facilitated in accordance with applicable laws and the rights of custodians and rights holders. Wherever legally permissible, manuscripts and associated metadata may be made available for public and scholarly research through the National Digital Repository, while sensitive, restricted or rights-protected materials may be subject to appropriate access conditions.

 

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

***

2289920.title: Manuscript Clusters and Partner Institutions under Gyan Bharatam   Initiative
2289920.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Manuscript Clusters and Partner Institutions under Gyan Bharatam   Initiative
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Gyan Bharatam Mission (GBM) has been mandated to establish a nation-wide network of Cluster Centers (CCs) and Independent Centers (ICs) across the country. These institutions have been selected based on prescribed criteria, including the size and significance of manuscript collections, institutional capacity, availability of qualified manpower and infrastructure, regional representation, and experience in manuscript-related activities. A list of CCs/ICs onboarded so far is at annexure.

National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported. The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is over 8 lakhs, out of which, more than 3.90 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access in view mode.

Gyan Bharatam, is a Pan-India initiative covering cataloguing, conservation, digitization and publication of manuscripts identified across the country. For effective implementation, a framework of Cluster Centres and Independent Centres has been envisaged. These centres are provided financial assistance in form of grant-in-aid to undertake manuscript related activities as elaborated above. The list of onboarded centers in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana is at annexure.

Gyan Bharatam envisages the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, research, publication and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage irrespective of script, language, dialect, tradition, community or geographical location. Eligible repositories having manuscripts are considered for onboarding with GBM in accordance with the Mission guidelines, subject to physical verification, institutional readiness and availability of resources, funds etc.

2289907.title: Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates CWG 2026 bronze medal-winner powerlifter Jhandu Kumar
2289907.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2289907.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates CWG 2026 bronze medal-winner powerlifter Jhandu Kumar
The para powerlifter received INR 10 Lakh cash award from Hon’ble Union Sports Minister; Jhandu said he was overjoyed when Hon’ble Prime Minister congratulated him on social media for his performance
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya felicitated para powerlifter Jhandu Kumar, who won India’s first medal in the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, at his residence on Monday. Jhandu won bronze in the men’s heavyweight category with a best lift of 190kg.

Dr Mandaviya handed INR 10 Lakh as cash award to Jhandu, who comes from a humble background in Nalanda district in Bihar. Talking about his experience of meeting the Union Sports Minister, the powerlifter said: “I felt privileged to meet the Union Sports Minister today. How many people get to meet a central minister in their lifetime. I never wondered that I will be felicitated for my achievement in sports. Dr Mandaviya asked me about my experience in Scotland. It was a great feeling to interact with him.”


 

Jhandu sold vegetables and even rode an e-rickshaw to support his family in Harnaut town of Nalanda before being selected by chief para coach Rajender Rahelu to train at SAI NCOE Gandhinagar back in June 2023. 

He said that when Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted about his achievement on social media, it gave him goosebumps. “I have not had much sleep since the time I have won a medal, due to the excitement and adrenaline rush. My phone has been buzzing throughout. I was overwhelmed when our Hon’ble PM wrote about me on social media. I think Indian sports has reached this level all thanks to his continuous encouragement and support for athletes. I think I was the only CWG medallist who received encouragement from his country’s Prime Minister,” the 29-year-old said.

Prior to his Glasgow glory, the powerlifter won back-to-back silver and gold medals in the Khelo India Para Games 2024 and 2025 editions respectively. The Khelo India athlete has now trained his eyes on the upcoming Asian Para Games scheduled from October 18 to 24, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. 

“When you receive such support and backing from the country’s leadership, you get motivated to perform even better. I will go to my hometown for a brief period to meet my family members before returning to Gandhinagar in order to prepare for Asian Para Games. China are a strong contender but I will do my best to secure a medal for my country, I promise,” Jhandu signed off.

*****

Ayushman Kumar

2289902.title: NHAI Successfully Defends Major Arbitration Case to Safeguard Public Funds in National Highway Projects
2289902.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Successfully Defends Major Arbitration Case to Safeguard Public Funds in National Highway Projects
Against claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores raised by the concessionaire, the Arbitral Tribunal awarded only Rs. 46 crores plus applicable interest to settle the case
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

Achieving a significant legal and financial milestone, NHAI has secured a favorable outcome in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a concessionaire promoted by M/s Era Infra Engineering Limited for 151 km long Bareilly – Sitapur BOT (Toll) project in Uttar Pradesh which was terminated by NHAI in May 2019. The Arbitral Tribunal substantially upheld the position of NHAI, thereby safeguarding public resources and reaffirming the contractual framework governing National Highway projects.

The three-member Arbitral Tribunal examined claims and counterclaims arising out of the concession agreement for the project. The Concessionaire had raised 30 claims aggregating to around Rs. 3,177 crores. After detailed consideration, the Tribunal allowed only three claims amounting to Rs. 46 crore plus applicable interest, while rejecting majority of the claims.

Arbitration Tribunal upheld the Supplementary Agreement (SA) dated 30th March 2015 and decided that project delays were concurrent and majority of the Concessionaire's claims were rejected.  NHAI also filed counterclaims, including claims relating to financial losses and public inconvenience. While these counterclaims were not allowed by the Tribunal, NHAI successfully defended itself against the overwhelming financial claims raised by the Concessionaire, resulting in a substantial protection of public funds.

In a series of recent notable legal wins, NHAI has successfully defended various arbitration cases. In June 2026, arbitration case related to Tumkur–Chitradurga 6 laning Project in Karnataka, was awarded in favour of NHAI for Rs. 1,202 crores. Also in April 2026, two arbitration cases in Panipat–Jalandhar Highway Project involving Concessionaire’s claims of around Rs. 8,375 Crores and counterclaims of NHAI for Rs. 2,888.64 Crores were settled for Rs. 819.96 Crores in favour of NHAI.  Similarly in May 2026, arbitration case related to 6 laning of Kamrej–Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat in which claims of around Rs. 174.49 crore raised by the contractor, was settled for only Rs. 54 lakhs by the Arbitral Tribunal.

The successful outcome of arbitration cases underscores NHAI's focus on robust contractual management and effective legal strategy. It also reinforces NHAI’s resolve to ensure effective utilisation of public funds while maintaining transparency and contractual discipline in the development and management of National Highway infrastructure.

***

GDH/DS

2289900.title: Digital Skill Development Platform
2289900.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2289900.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Digital Skill Development Platform
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has developed Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for the skilling ecosystem under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). Launched on 13th September 2023, it brings the entire skilling ecosystem onto a single unified platform, integrating training, assessment, certification, employment and entrepreneurship services, while allowing training providers, employers and government schemes to onboard onto a common interoperable ecosystem. Built on a mobile-first approach and interoperable with other Government platforms such as National Career Service, eShram, DigiLocker and BHASHINI, SIDH advances the Government's vision of a unified, citizen-centric skilling ecosystem accessible to all.

 

As per Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) data, a total of 35,17,023 learners are registered under PMKVY 4.0, 52,98,397 under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), 10,19,992under the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme, and 4,96,755 under the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative. A total of 78,647 trainers holding a valid Trainer ID are registered on the platform. Further, 13,633 training centres are registered under PMKVY 4.0 (Short Term Training and Special Projects), 296 training centres under the JSS scheme, and 13,888 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) are onboarded on SIDH. The key courses available on the platform span short-term skilling and apprenticeship programmes under PMKVY 4.0 and NAPS, community-based training under JSS, and foundational and applied Artificial Intelligence courses under SOAR. The number of youth registered, trained/oriented, certified and employed through the platform, State/UT wise, including in Punjab, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, particularly Nabarangpur and Bastar Lok Sabha Constituencies, is given at Annexure-A.

 

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), has launched the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative to equip learners, educators and the workforce with foundational Artificial Intelligence (AI) knowledge and practical competencies. The initiative comprises nationally recognised, NSQF-aligned, fully online and self-paced AI courses delivered through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) by NCVET-recognised Awarding Bodies. Subsequently, SOAR has been expanded beyond foundational AI literacy to include AI and AI application-oriented courses focused on AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualised AI applications for the informal sector. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 4,96,426 learners have enrolled and 98,576 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH).

 

The Government has undertaken several measures to ensure effective access to digital skilling platforms, including the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), for citizens across rural, remote and aspirational districts. SIDH serves as a one-stop digital platform for accessing skilling, certification, apprenticeship and employment-related opportunities through a single interface.

 

To facilitate wider outreach and accessibility, the Government has adopted an integrated online and offline approach, including multilingual awareness campaigns, digital outreach, community mobilisation through Panchayats and Common Service Centres, workshops, skill awareness activities and on-ground support initiatives. District Skill Committees are also involved in identifying local skilling requirements and facilitating training opportunities in rural and underserved areas. Further, initiatives such as Skill Hubs under PMKVY 4.0 and the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme provide skill training opportunities closer to the beneficiaries, including in aspirational, backward and remote regions.

 

To strengthen AI-based skill development and digital training infrastructure, the Government is promoting skilling in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Cloud Computing, Internet of Things, Data Analytics, Cyber Security and Green Technologies. Digital and blended learning models, industry partnerships and continuous upskilling and reskilling initiatives are being promoted to ensure access to industry-relevant and future-ready skills across the country.

 

Further, the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative has been designed as a fully online, self-paced AI learning programme to promote AI-enabled learning across the country through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH). The courses are NSQF-aligned and credit-linked under the National Credit Framework (NCrF), with credits being integrated with the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) to facilitate transparent recognition and accumulation of learning outcomes. This enables learners to access nationally recognised AI courses from anywhere in the country while promoting portability, transparency and lifelong learning within the skilling ecosystem.

2289894.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2289894.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Salient Features of Naps-2
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India launched ‘National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme’ (NAPS) in August, 2016 with the objective to promote apprenticeship training and to increase the engagement of apprentices. Since 2022-23, the scheme continues as NAPS-2 and implemented throughout the country.

Under NAPS-2, the Government provides partial stipend support to apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961. The Government's share of stipend is transferred directly to the bank accounts of apprentices through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism, ensuring transparency and timely disbursement.

Based on representations received from establishments, State Governments and Sector Skill Councils, and considering the increase in the cost of living, the proposal for revision of minimum stipend rates linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) was considered and approved by the Central Apprenticeship Council (CAC) in its 38th meeting held on 26.05.2025. The revised stipend rates were subsequently notified through Gazette Notification dated 11.09.2025.

The salient features of NAPS-2 are as follows:

 

  1. Financial support through DBT: Government provides stipend support to eligible apprentices engaged by establishments under the Apprentices Act, 1961, with the Government's share being released directly to beneficiaries through a Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism to ensure transparency and timely disbursement.
  2. Industry-led training: Apprenticeship training is conducted in actual work environments using the training facilities available with participating establishments, enabling hands-on learning and industry exposure.
  3. Technology-enabled implementation: A dedicated online portal,www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in, facilitates end-to-end implementation of apprenticeship training, including registration, contract approval, monitoring and disbursement ofbenefits.
  4. Facilitation through TPAs: Mobilisation of apprentices and establishments, particularly MSMEs, is supported through empanelled ThirdParty Aggregators (TPAs).
  5. Awareness and outreach initiatives: Regular organization of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) to create awareness and facilitate apprenticeship engagement.

 

A total of 52,98,397 apprentices have been engaged under NAPS across the country from FY 2018-19 till FY 2026-27 (Upto 30th June 2026).Further, 57,945 establishments have been registered on the apprenticeship portal, of which, 38,936 are MSMEs. State/UT-wise details of apprentices engaged and establishments participating under the scheme, including district wise details for Karnataka are placed at Tables-I & II of the Annexure. 

The details of government share of stipend support disbursed through DBT, which was started from July 2023,under the scheme, including Karnataka is placed at Table-III of the Annexure.

A third-party evaluation of NAPS conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) indicates positive employment outcomes under the scheme. The study reported that around 72% of apprentices were offered full-time employment after completion of apprenticeship training. The findings further indicate that apprenticeship serves as an effective pathway for transition from training to employment, with significant improvement in income levels and employability outcomes among apprentices.

The Government is organizing Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Mela (PMNAM) as a monthly event in various locations across the country since the month of June 2022. States/UTs have been advised to organize PMNAM every 2nd Monday in 1/3 of total number of districts every month with the flexibility for choosing the district/location and the day of Mela based on local conditions/festivals, etc. so that all districts are covered once in every quarter, and four times in a year.

Since June 2022, 7,370 PMNAMs organized across the country. In Karnataka, 156 PMNAMs have been conducted. State/UT-wise details of PMNAMs conducted and candidates engaged thereunder are placed at Table IV of the Annexure.

The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages greater integration of vocational education with mainstream education and promotes seamless mobility between academic and vocational pathways. In line with this vision, the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), developed in collaboration with UGC and AICTE, enables students enrolled in degree and diploma programmes to undertake apprenticeship training as an integral part of their curriculum. The programme enhances employability, promotes outcome-based learning, strengthens industry-academia linkages and facilitates acquisition of industry-relevant skills.

Further, apprenticeship training in establishments is offered through both Designated Trades and Optional Trades. The Government is also promoting apprenticeship opportunities in emerging and high-growth sectors such as Information Technology (IT), biotechnology, renewable energy, electronics, semiconductors, drones, logistics and other sunrise sectors.

2289890.title: Skilling for Space and Geospatial Sectors
2289890.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2289890.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Skilling for Space and Geospatial Sectors
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Andhra Pradesh. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.

The Government is actively promoting skill development in the space and geospatial emerging technology sectors through flagship schemes of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), namely the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), which impart short-term skilling, up-skilling, re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), and structured on-the-job apprenticeship training in areas such as GIS, spatial data management, drone technology, software development, telecommunications, and electronics. Furthermore, to strengthen the capacity of Non-Government Entities (NGEs) and academia, IN-SPACe under the Department of Space has introduced 11 short-term skill development courses in space technology, under which over 1,000 candidates have been successfully trained across the country.

The State/UT-wise number of candidates trained and apprentices engaged in space and geospatial related sectors during the last three years as well as the number of training centres/establishments under PMKVY and NAPS are provided at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively. The details of HEIs conducting various space technology courses across the country are given at Annexure-III.

District Skill Committees (DSCs), established across all States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh are mandated with formulating District Skill Development Plans (DSDPs) to support decentralized, grassroots-level skill planning by identifying local employment opportunities, skilling demand, and available training infrastructure. Government skill programmes are then designed to bridge these identified skill gaps across sectors. The Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry experts, regularly conduct skill gap studies to assess sector-wise skill needs and set competency standards, which guide government interventions to align the workforce with industry requirements. Additionally, the SANKALP (Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion)-supported National Skill Gap Study by National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) provides a standardized, data-driven framework to assess skill gaps across seven high-growth sectors. It helps MSDE align skilling initiatives with industry demand and future workforce needs. Also, IN-SPACe has carried out an assessment of the skilling requirements in areas like space technology, launch vehicle, rockets, satellites etc. in consultation with the industry and has undertaken the development of relevant course curricula on the basis of the identified needs.

To expand outreach and strengthen the linkage between skilling and employment, the Government has been organizing Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) since June 2022, along with awareness generation, employer outreach, and candidate mobilization activities. Through collaboration with employers, industry bodies, educational institutions, and Sector Skill Councils, the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) facilitates the acquisition of industry-relevant skills and enhances employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for youth, including those from rural areas. Further, the faculties for short-term skill developments in IN-SPACe are from ISRO, IN-SPACe, Ex-ISRO officers, private space entities/start-ups/academic institutions for delivering the lecture and for covering practical aspects during the course.

In order to align skill development programs with the industrial requirements in the emerging sectors including the space and geospatial sectors, and to facilitate partnerships with private entities/academic institutions, to improve the employability of the skilled manpower and entrepreneurship opportunities, the following specific steps have been taken by MSDE across the country including Andhra Pradesh:

 

  1. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space.
  2. The Awarding Bodies recognised by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations.
  3. NCVET has approved 10,209 qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of which 2,975 qualifications are valid and active, and 7,234 qualifications are archived.
  4. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have been set up which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to determine skill competency standards.
  5. Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE is implementing Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) which are meant to provide training to ITI students in industrial environment as per their requirements.
  6. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially aligned with Industry 4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for upcoming market demand and industry requirements.
  7. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.
  8. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern technologies.
  9. Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode, provide training to create a pool of industry-ready workforce for Industry, equipped with cutting-edge technology and hands-on training.
  10. Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are organised to facilitate the placements and apprenticeship opportunities to the certified candidates.

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Artificial Intelligence and Skill India Initiatives
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills including emerging technologies.

PMKVY 4.0 implemented since FY 2022-23 gives special emphasis on future skills and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Robotics, Cloud Computing, Internet of Things (IoT), Data Analytics, Cyber Security and Green Technologies, to prepare youth for new and emerging job roles.

The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE), has developed 170 NSQF-compliant courses, including 32 new-age/Future Skills courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Robotics, Cyber Security, and Green Skills, etc. These courses are designed to equip youth across the country with industry-relevant skills in emerging technologies, enhance their employability, and meet the evolving demand for skilled manpower across various sectors. These courses are delivered through a nationwide network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs).

The number of candidates trained under Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technology-related skilling programmes, year and State/UT-wise, is at Annexure.

Under PMKVY 1.0 to PMKVY 3.0, which were implemented during FY-2015-16 to FY 2021-23, a total of 1.11 Crore candidates were certified, out of which 24.38 lakhs were reported placed under the Short Term Training (STT) component of the scheme. Further, under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career paths, and they are suitably oriented for the same. Hence, placements are not monitored under PMKVY 4.0.

Skill Gap studies are conducted from time to time to assess the industry demand and the employability of the candidates trained under various Skill India initiatives in various sectors. Such studies guide the interventions of the Government aimed at preparing the workforce as per the industry needs. Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) have undertaken skill gap studies across sectors such as Electronics, Logistics, Advance Manufacturing, etc. providing demand–supply assessments and manpower projections.

Further, to synergize initiatives of skill development in the country and to fulfil the regional skill requirements, the schemes of MSDE focus on implementation of training interventions with participation of States and Districts through State Skill Development Mission (SSDMs) and District Skill Committees (DSCs). DSCs identify sectors with employment opportunities as well as the associated demand for skilling in the district, and map the available facilities for Skill Training. The SANKALP (Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion) scheme also supported a National Skill Gap Study by National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), that provided a standardized, data-driven framework to assess skill gaps across seven high-growth sectors including computer programming activities under the IT sector. The skill gap studies help the Government to align the skilling initiatives with industry demand and future workforce needs across the country. Skill Development Programmes of the Government are designed and implemented to bridge identified skill gaps across sectors.

To reduce the employability gap of candidates trained under skill development programs, the following specific steps have been taken by MSDE:

 

  1. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space.
  2. The Awarding Bodies recognized by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations.
  3. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have been set up which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to determine skill competency standards.
  4. Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE is implementing Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) which are meant to provide training to ITI students in industrial environment as per their requirements.
  5. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially aligned with Industry 4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for upcoming market demand and industry requirements.
  6. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.
  7. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern technologies.
  8. Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode, provide training to create a pool of industry-ready workforce for Industry, equipped with cutting-edge technology and hands-on training.
  9. Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are organised to facilitate placements and apprenticeship opportunities to the certified candidates.
  10. The Government has launched PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a centrally sponsored scheme with an investment of Rs.60,000 crore. The scheme envisages the upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs across the country in a hub-and-spoke model comprising 200 hub ITIs and 800 spoke ITIs. PM-SETU focuses on improving employability outcomes through industry-led governance, and indirectly supports self-employment and entrepreneurship by enabling learners (including early-stage enterprises and first-time entrepreneurs) to acquire industry-relevant skills, gain exposure to real work environments, and access career guidance, placement support, and self-employment support through strengthened institutional systems and industry linkages.

Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:52PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Kasaragod. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills, including for the maritime sector.

Some of the initiatives taken to promote skilling in the maritime sector include:

 

  1. Under PMKVY, training is imparted in logistics and maritime-related job roles such as Documentation Assistant, Consignment Booking Assistant, Consignment Tracking Executive, Courier Delivery Executive, Signalman Port Operation, Vessel Operator Grade-1, Marine Capture Fisherman and Protective & Marine Painter, among others. In Kasaragod district of Kerala, 240 candidates have been trained/oriented under PMKVY, out of which 197 candidates are certified.
  2. The Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) has approved 171 Maritime Training Institutes (MTIs) in India. The employment of seafarers on Indian or Foreign Ships depends on their training, assessment and certification in accordance with the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW Convention) of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) for the seafarers, to which India is a signatory.
  3. The DGS has also issued a list of approved maritime training courses. All these courses are to be in line with the Model Course issued by the IMO and the STCW Convention, 2010. The Training, Examination and Assessment Programme (TEAP) manual has also been issued by the DGS, providing necessary guidelines and details of the training courses, seagoing services and examination. Besides these, there is a common course for faculties of the Maritime Training Institutes (MTIs), namely Vertical Integration Course for Trainers.
  4. Additionally, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has initiated various steps for promoting skill development, including for coastal youth in the ports, shipping, and waterways sector by strengthening maritime education and training, upgrading the curriculum of maritime institutes, and enhancing industry-oriented skill programmes in the port sector and logistics. These efforts aim to create a globally competitive, skilled workforce to support India's maritime growth. Some of these steps are as under:

 

  1. 11 shipyards have signed MoUs with 34 ITIs across 8 coastal States towards implementation of On Job Training (OJT) of 150 hours.
  2. Training of Trainers (ToT) program has been implemented at 2 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in West Bengal by Centre of Excellence in Maritime and Shipbuilding (CEMS).
  3. A preliminary Skill Gap Study has been completed across 9 shipyards.
  4. Indian Ship Technology Centre (ISTC) has been established as a Section 8 company to facilitate skilling.
  5. A Plan of Implementation (PoI) has been signed between MoPSW and Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) for a skill development project in the shipbuilding sector.

 

Government has taken several measures to improve employment opportunities for youth, including those from coastal areas that include (i) Providing industry-aligned skilling through PMKVY and other skill development initiatives (ii) Offering training in diverse sectors including logistics, port operations, warehousing, supply chain management and marine-related job roles (iii) Aligning courses with National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) based Qualification Packs developed in consultation with industry (iv) Promoting Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for workers possessing existing skills (v) Encouraging linkage of trained candidates with employment opportunities through industry partnerships and placement facilitation and others. These initiatives aim to enhance the employability of youth in coastal regions and support manpower requirements in maritime, logistics and allied sectors.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

2289882.title: 33 out of the 37 State/UT Legislatures have signed MoUs for the implementation of the National e-Vidhan Application
2289882.body_html:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
33 out of the 37 State/UT Legislatures have signed MoUs for the implementation of the National e-Vidhan Application
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi

33 out of the 37 State/UT Legislatures have signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) for the implementation of the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA). Out of these, 21 Legislative Houses have been transformed into digital Legislatures under the NeVA project. The digitalisation of the two Houses of Parliament is outside the scope of the NeVA project.

 NeVA has improved the efficiency of legislative functioning by enabling electronic processing of house business. It has reduced dependence on paper-based procedures, facilitated faster processing and dissemination of legislative business, improved accessibility of legislative information, and resulted in cost savings in printing, handling and storage of documents.

A mid-term evaluation of the NeVA project has been undertaken by NITI Aayog. The evaluation report, inter alia, observed that NeVA has reduced paper usage and improved legislative workflows. Enhanced coordination among Legislatures and Government Departments has facilitated quicker processing of legislative business and the public portal of NeVA provides real-time access to legislative documents. The report also noted that capacity-building initiatives, including establishment of NeVA Seva Kendras, have supported adoption of the platform by providing technical assistance and training to stakeholders.

The NeVA application is upgraded from time to time based on user feedback and operational requirements.

The NeVA application has been migrated to the secure NIC MeghRaj 2.0 cloud infrastructure to enhance cybersecurity. Integration with BHASHINI has enabled text-to-text translation of public portal content, improving linguistic accessibility. The application has been designed as a device-agnostic platform to ensure interoperability across devices. Role based dashboards, workflow based electronic processing of legislative documents, etc. ensure coordination between different user roles such as Members, Secretariat of Legislatures and Government Departments.

This information was given by the Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2289881.body_html:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
NeVA has improved the efficiency of legislative functioning through digitization
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi

33 out of the 37 State/UT Legislatures have signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) for implementation of the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA). Out of these, 21 Legislative Houses have been transformed into digital Legislatures under the NeVA project.

The NeVA Project is funded as per the CSS pattern with a total project outlay of Rs.673.94 crore, of which the Central Government's share is limited to Rs.423.60 crore. An amount of Rs.23,58,20,600/-  has been sanctioned for implementation of the NeVA Project in the two Houses of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature. Necessary technical support is provided to all participating State/UT Legislatures, including Andhra Pradesh, through the Central Project Management Unit (CPMU) in the form of capacity-building initiatives.

As per the mid-term evaluation of the NeVA Project, NeVA has improved the efficiency of legislative functioning through digitization of legislative processes, reduced dependence on paper-based procedures, faster processing and dissemination of legislative business, and improved accessibility of legislative information. It has also led to savings in printing, handling and storage of documents.

State/UT Legislatures are autonomous institutions. Accordingly, NeVA Project has been implemented in consultation with the respective State Legislatures, subject to their preparedness.

This information was given by the Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2289858.title: National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa and MDNIY Launch Yoga Wellness Instructor Certificate Course in Leh
2289858.body_html:
AYUSH
National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa and MDNIY Launch Yoga Wellness Instructor Certificate Course in Leh
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi

A three-month (400-hour) Yoga Wellness Instructor Certificate Course has been launched at the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR), Leh. The course is being conducted in collaboration with the Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), New Delhi, and the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa, Leh, in accordance with the course guidelines of MDNIY.

The course was formally inaugurated by Ven. Bhikkhu Sanghasena, Prime Minister Yoga Awardee and Founder President of the Mahabodhi International Meditation Centre (MIMC). Dr. Tashi Thinlas, Director, Department of Ayush, Health & Medical Education, UT Ladakh, attended the event as the Guest of Honour. The inaugural session was presided over by Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR), Leh.

Dr. Padma Gurmet congratulated the participants on joining the first-ever Yoga Wellness Certificate Course in Ladakh. He encouraged the students to make the best use of the opportunity by actively participating in both the theoretical and practical components of the training programme. He also expressed gratitude to Ven. Bhikkhu Sanghasena for his efforts in promoting Yoga and Meditation in Ladakh for the well-being of citizens and reiterated NISR's commitment to promoting traditional health systems and wellness practices for the benefit of society.

Dr. Tashi Thinlas appreciated the efforts of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa in promoting holistic healthcare and wellness through yoga education. He emphasized the growing significance of integrating Modern Medicine, Traditional Medicine and Yoga to achieve overall health and well-being. He also highlighted the scope of Yoga therapists in the Union Territory of Ladakh and the plan to incorporate Yoga in the health sector.

Ven. Bhikkhu Sanghasena highlighted yoga as a way of life that nurtures physical health, mental peace and spiritual well-being. He encouraged the students to embrace yoga with sincerity and dedication for their personal growth and to contribute towards a healthier society. He also invited the students and faculty to visit the Mahabodhi Meditation Centre during the course for meditation, stating that Yoga and Meditation go hand in hand.

Earlier, Shri Gopal Sharma, Course Coordinator, briefed the students on the programme schedule and course guidelines. The inaugural programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Ms. Dolma Tsering, formally marking the formal commencement of the three-month Yoga Wellness Instructor Certificate Course for the newly enrolled participants.

2289853.title: How Madanapalle is building a Zero Waste City
2289853.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
How Madanapalle is building a Zero Waste City
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi

Driven by the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, Madanapalle Municipality is reshaping urban sanitation through scientific waste management and sustainable resource recovery.

Madanapalle Municipality in Andhra Pradesh is strengthening its urban sanitation and solid waste management systems through scientific and sustainable practices. In response to rapid urban growth and increasing waste generation, the municipality has adopted a structured and integrated approach focused on waste segregation, scientific processing and resource recovery, with the objective of developing Madanapalle into a ‘Zero Waste City.’

Madanapalle generates approx.. 62 TPD of municipal solid waste, including 25.50 TPD of dry waste, 36 TPD of wet waste and 0.50 TPD of domestic hazardous waste. To ensure efficient management of this waste stream, a systematic source segregation mechanism has been implemented across the town. Waste is categorized into biodegradable, non-biodegradable and upcycling waste, facilitating scientific processing, improved recycling practices and environmentally sustainable disposal in alignment with the objectives of SBM-U 2.0.


 

A major focus area for the municipality has been scientific management of biodegradable waste through decentralized and sustainable practices. Bulk Waste Generators are being encouraged to establish on-site composting systems, while citizens are adopting home composting and terrace gardening to manage wet waste at source. Every day, nearly 15.50 tonnes of wet waste is processed through windrow composting at the municipal compost yard, generating around 4.65 tonnes of compost used for parks, plantations, and gardening activities across the town. Additionally, around 3 tonnes of wet waste is processed daily through vermi composting, producing nearly 1.20 tonnes of nutrient-rich compost, further reducing landfill burden and promoting sustainable waste utilization.

 

 

Dry waste generated in the town is systematically segregated into recyclable and non-recyclable categories at the doorstep level. Recyclable materials are sent to the Material Recovery Facility (MRF), where they are processed and channelled to authorized recycling units for resource recovery.

Non-recyclable waste is transported to cement factories for co-processing. This initiative not only improves waste utilization efficiency but also helps generate additional revenue for the municipality. By ensuring proper segregation at source, Madanapalle has enhanced the calorific value of recyclable waste and minimized the quantity of mixed waste reaching disposal sites.

Through door-to-door collection drives and the operational Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (RRR) Centre, the municipality collects items such as e-waste, old clothes, toys, books, and footwear. These materials are repaired, reused, or redistributed among slum communities, homeless individuals, and old age homes.

The city has also adopted creative waste-to-art initiatives using discarded tyre waste. Public spaces and parks are being beautified with artistic installations made from waste materials, promoting environmental awareness while contributing to the vision of zero dumping.

 

Madanapallehas successfully remediated nearly 36,512 metric tonnes of legacy waste through bio-mining and bio-remediation, reclaiming around 9.40 acres of land. Nearly 5 acres of the reclaimed area has been developed through plantation activities, transforming former dumpsites into green urban spaces. Recovered materials such as Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) are being sent to cement plants for co-processing, while soil and inert materials are reused for filling low-lying areas, promoting scientific waste utilization and environmental improvement.

Wall paintings and murals promoting cleanliness, waste segregation, and hygiene have transformed public spaces into vibrant awareness platforms. The Waste-to-Art Park at NVR Layout stands as a symbol of innovation and sustainability, showcasing how discarded materials can be creatively repurposed into functional and aesthetic public installations.

Aligned with the vision of the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, Madanapalle is steadily progressing towards becoming a Zero Dump and Zero Littering City through strong administrative leadership, scientific waste management systems, and active community participation. The municipality’s integrated approach—encompassing composting, recycling, upcycling, biomining, legacy waste remediation, and citizen engagement—demonstrates how urban local bodies can build sustainable and environmentally responsible cities.

2289851.title: INSTITUTIONAL OUTREACH BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITIES
2289851.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
INSTITUTIONAL OUTREACH BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITIES
Posted On: 27 JUL 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi

NCM has conducted a study on the subject “Contribution of Jain Community in the Field of Education” during 2026. The study documents the historical evolution, institutional contribution and educational philosophy of the Jain community in India. It captures the role of Jain trusts, philanthropists, educational institutions and community organisations in promoting learning, research, scholarships, value-based education and inclusive access to education.

National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in discharge of its advisory and facilitative mandate, organized Conference of State Minorities Commissions on 19 May 2026 at New Delhi, which was attended by representatives of State Minorities Commissions, along with officials of State Governments and Union Territories. The Conference served as a platform to deliberate on institutional strengthening, administrative coordination, grievance redressal mechanisms, and the exchange of best practices for enhancing outreach and improving the delivery of welfare measures for minority communities.

Annexure

 

Annexure to part(a) of Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No 912 for answer on 27.07.2026 on the subject “Institutional Outreach by the National Commission for Minorities”

Details of the seminars, conference and outreach progammes organized by National Commission for Minorities during 2026

  1. National Seminar on "Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways" (27.02.2026, New Delhi)

The National Commission for Minorities (NCM) organized a national seminar on “Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways” on 27.02.2026 in New Delhi. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar focused on heritage preservation, education, youth engagement and the role of Buddhist philosophy in promoting peace and social harmony. The seminar brought together policymakers, scholars, spiritual leaders, and community representatives to deliberate on the evolving role of Buddhism in India’s socio-cultural landscape.

  1. National Seminar on "The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education and Philanthropy" (23.04.2026, Indore)

National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in collaboration with Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV), Indore, organized a National Seminar on “The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education, and Philanthropy” on 23.4.2026 in Indore. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar brought together scholars, academicians, industrialists, philanthropists, students, and members of the Jain community to discuss the community’s significant role in nation-building.

  1. National Seminar on "Parsis in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Socio-Economic Pathways" (09.05.2026, Mumbai)

National Commission for Minorities (NCM) organized a National Seminar on “Parsis in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Socio-Economic Pathways” on 09.05.2026 in Mumbai. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar focused on the preservation of Parsi heritage, socio-economic development, demographic challenges and the community's invaluable contribution to nation-building. The seminar brought together ministers, policymakers, scholars, industrialists, academicians, and members of the Parsi community to discuss issues related to cultural preservation, demographic challenges, and socio-economic development.

  1. Conference of State Minorities Commissions (19.05.2026, New Delhi)

National Commission for Minorities organized the Conference of State Minorities Commissions on 19th May 2026 at New Delhi to discuss minority welfare, protection of minority rights and inclusive development. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The Conference deliberated on best practices, challenges faced by State Commissions and the role of minority communities in nation-building. The conference brought together representatives from State Minorities Commissions, State Governments, Union Territories and minority communities to strengthen coordination and welfare mechanisms across the country.

 

This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

PMJVK is a demand-driven Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS). Accordingly, no State-wise or Union Territory-wise budgetary allocation is made under the Scheme. Funds are released based on eligible project proposals received from the States/UTs and their fulfilment of the prescribed guidelines and conditions.

(d)        No instance of poor quality work has been flagged in any third-party quality assurance audit conducted under the PMJVK Scheme.

(e)        Yes, Sir. The Ministry has commissioned independent third-party studies to assess the implementation and impact of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK).

An Evaluation Study was conducted by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), New Delhi, and an Impact-cum-Assessment Study was carried out by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog. These studies provided evidence-based assessments of the scheme's implementation, impact, efficiency and sustainability in Minority Concentration Areas. They examined infrastructure creation, service delivery and outcomes, while also identifying areas for improvement, including awareness generation, fund flow, monitoring and maintenance of assets.

The IIPA evaluation primarily focused on assessing the physical progress and impact of PMJVK projects. Further, to institutionalize independent technical oversight, Third Party Quality Assurance (TPQA) has been made mandatory for all PMJVK projects across States and Union Territories.
